A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FonTS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–G are readable and matchable despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original text-rendering experiments, component ablations, qualitative comparisons, and a 22-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a prefix ablation and quantitative dataset-quality assessment.

M1.justification: TC-FT, ETC-tokens, SCA, objectives, and training stages remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 newly documents inference-time handling of the existing 'sks' prefix; it does not establish that the underlying method changed from v2.

E1.justification: Appendix E newly evaluates images from TWD and Posta alongside SC-artext and SC-general. This modestly extends dataset coverage for quality assessment; the training corpora and BTR, ATR, and MARIO rendering coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The rendering comparisons retain the same methods, including Glyph-ByT5, TD-2, SD3, Flux, IP-Adapter variants, Redux, AnyText, and Midjourney. TWD and Posta enter as dataset comparisons, without evidence that their rendering methods were newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The new dataset assessment specifies 100 randomly sampled images per dataset and Q-Align aesthetic/quality scoring. Appendix B.4 also adds an inference comparison with versus without 'sks'. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets, and user-study settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.4 and Figure 22 test whether omitting 'sks' at inference alleviates scene-text detachment. Appendix E adds a comparative dataset-quality analysis. Earlier TC-FT, ETC-token, and SCA ablations remain present.

E5.justification: Fixed-seed comparisons and the illustrated seeds 0–3 in the T5 ablation are retained. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run aggregate uncertainty; the new dataset sample size changes evaluation design, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables retain their values. New Table 13 reports aesthetic/quality scores of 42.64/55.83 for TWD, 47.23/64.89 for Posta, 68.57/88.73 for SC-artext, and 84.78/91.20 for SC-general. Figure 22 adds qualitative detachment results, and Figure 30 adds dataset examples; these are additions rather than improved scores on retained benchmarks.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, parameter-change definitions, and attention equations (1–5) are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain first word-level typography control, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, text-agnostic style control, a controllable dataset, and superior font/style consistency. The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 discusses language drift from extended training and limited regularization. v3 additionally explains that omitting the training prefix at inference can alleviate scene-text detachment, supported by Figure 22. Other mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications, and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents omitting 'sks' at inference and replaces the abstract's future dataset/model-release statement with a project-page link. The PDFs do not establish an actual resource release. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and dataset-construction details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands cited coverage of controllable generation, including existing DiT control/editing systems and additional typography work such as EasyText and WordCon. It explicitly positions FonTS as advancing existing DiT control research. Appendix E also introduces TWD, Posta, and Q-Align references.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar corrections, rewrites the controllable-generation discussion, rephrases non-token prompt examples, revises the author block, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact, with B.4 added.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 22 and 30 and Table 13, changes Figure 21's prompt labels, and redistributes existing displays. The former Figure 22 becomes an enlarged Figure 23. Existing result images are retained, and the general two-column presentation remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.4 provides useful inference guidance and evidence addressing the previously acknowledged detachment problem, while Appendix E adds quantitative support for dataset-quality choices. These improve reproducibility and supporting evidence modestly. The core method and benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new qualitative prefix analysis does not establish resolution of the broader language-drift limitation.
